bounded_hypotheses.statement: The initial local formation may have been too broad for timely mutual support against the enemy closing speed.
A protected tactical reserve may have been unavailable when the first local crisis developed.
Local units appear to enter the decisive area at different times rather than as one coordinated engagement.
Ranged and artillery effectiveness may have declined as friendly and enemy units became intermingled near rough terrain.
After the first unfavorable exchange, no clear regroup, fallback line, or asset-extraction state is visually apparent.

interpretation_limits: Observed command events would remain observation only and not acknowledgement.
Visible movement after a command is not causal execution proof.
The owner trace is not an optimal-policy label.
The visual diagnosis does not prove that any alternative would have produced victory.
Embedded replay strings are evidence of labels present in the binary, not a complete roster or deployment reconstruction.
telemetry_required: stable unit identity and full local/enemy hierarchy
health, model-count, fatigue, morale, and ammunition trajectories
first engagement, wavering, routing, rally, and shatter timestamps
exact command events, command targets, and inferred unit attribution
role-specific casualties, kills, travel, and threat exposure
battle completion marker, victorious alliance, and exact outcome evidence

visual_identity_facts.statement: The replay-selection screen visibly identifies An Ogre's Folly as a land battle.
The recording visibly identifies Reikland against Warhost of the Apocalypse, with The Empire and Warriors of Chaos race labels.
The recording does not show a normal result card, so the exact defeat grade is not visually observed.

visual_phase_windows.note: The Empire begins in a broad, shallow formation with substantial lateral separation.
Chaos pressure reaches the left and center quickly while much of the local line is not yet mutually supporting.
The pressured local group fights in congestion while other elements contribute unevenly or arrive piecemeal.
The battle separates into local fights rather than one mutually supporting formation.
More local units appear depleted, wavering, routing, or isolated without a visible fresh reserve.
Remaining local pockets withdraw or are surrounded while Chaos retains multiple combat-effective units.
